Modules.session_description_1: Introduces the role of risk management within project controls, linking governance, risk exposure and professional judgement to effective control decisions. Evidence: Risk context discussion, reflective notes and project controls risk scenario activity
Modules.session_description_2: Develops understanding of the end-to-end risk management process and how risk interfaces with cost, schedule, governance and control disciplines. Evidence: Risk process map and interface identification exercise
Modules.session_description_3: Builds practical capability in identifying credible risks, describing causes and consequences, and structuring a usable risk register for analysis and action. Evidence: Risk register build, risk statement quality review and prioritised risk log
Modules.session_description_4: Applies qualitative assessment techniques to prioritise risks in line with agreed appetite, thresholds and stakeholder expectations. Evidence: Probability and impact assessment, risk scoring matrix and prioritisation rationale
Modules.session_description_5: Introduces quantitative thinking, data interpretation and analytical methods used to support evidence-based project controls decisions. Evidence: Quantitative risk calculation exercises and interpretation notes
Modules.session_description_6: Explores schedule risk, logic quality, uncertainty, critical path implications and the impact of risk on realistic delivery forecasts. Evidence: Schedule risk review, logic assessment and schedule impact analysis
Modules.session_description_7: Develops understanding of cost uncertainty, contingency assessment and the relationship between risk exposure, budgets and control baselines. Evidence: Cost risk assessment, contingency justification and budget impact exercise
Modules.session_description_8: Strengthens integrated control practice by connecting cost, schedule and risk information to support coherent project performance reporting. Evidence: Integrated cost-schedule-risk analysis and control summary
Modules.session_description_9: Focuses on developing proportionate responses, assigning clear ownership and evaluating residual exposure after mitigation actions. Evidence: Risk response plan, ownership matrix and residual risk review

Modules.session_description_11: Links risk governance, assurance and reporting to stakeholder confidence, control discipline and accountable decision-making. Evidence: Risk report, governance review and assurance action log
Modules.session_description_12: Develops facilitation and continuous improvement practice by evaluating risk maturity and identifying improvements to risk management ways of working. Evidence: Risk maturity assessment, facilitated lessons session and improvement plan
Modules.session_description_13: Applies risk identification, qualitative and quantitative assessment, schedule risk and cost risk analysis within an integrated case scenario. Evidence: Case-based risk register, qualitative and quantitative analysis outputs, schedule and cost impact summary
Modules.session_description_14: Consolidates integrated risk reporting, governance, response planning, ownership, residual exposure and continuous improvement through applied case work. Evidence: Integrated risk control pack, governance briefing, response plan and improvement recommendations
Modules.session_names_json: ["Risk Management in the Project Controls Environment", "The Risk Management Process and Its Interfaces", "Risk Identification and Building a Credible Risk Register", "Qualitative Assessment, Prioritisation and Risk Appetite", "Quantitative Foundations for Risk Analysis", "Schedule Risk Analysis", "Cost Risk Analysis and Contingency", "Integrating Cost, Schedule and Risk", "Risk Responses, Ownership and Residual Exposure", "Biases, Heuristics and Decision Quality", "Risk Governance, Assurance and Reporting", "Risk Maturity, Facilitation and Continuous Improvement", "Case Workshop I", "Case Workshop II"]
Modules.session_descriptions_json: ["Introduces the role of risk management within project controls, linking governance, risk exposure and professional judgement to effective control decisions. Evidence: Risk context discussion, reflective notes and project controls risk scenario activity", "Develops understanding of the end-to-end risk management process and how risk interfaces with cost, schedule, governance and control disciplines. Evidence: Risk process map and interface identification exercise", "Builds practical capability in identifying credible risks, describing causes and consequences, and structuring a usable risk register for analysis and action. Evidence: Risk register build, risk statement quality review and prioritised risk log", "Applies qualitative assessment techniques to prioritise risks in line with agreed appetite, thresholds and stakeholder expectations. Evidence: Probability and impact assessment, risk scoring matrix and prioritisation rationale", "Introduces quantitative thinking, data interpretation and analytical methods used to support evidence-based project controls decisions. Evidence: Quantitative risk calculation exercises and interpretation notes", "Explores schedule risk, logic quality, uncertainty, critical path implications and the impact of risk on realistic delivery forecasts. Evidence: Schedule risk review, logic assessment and schedule impact analysis", "Develops understanding of cost uncertainty, contingency assessment and the relationship between risk exposure, budgets and control baselines. Evidence: Cost risk assessment, contingency justification and budget impact exercise", "Strengthens integrated control practice by connecting cost, schedule and risk information to support coherent project performance reporting. Evidence: Integrated cost-schedule-risk analysis and control summary", "Focuses on developing proportionate responses, assigning clear ownership and evaluating residual exposure after mitigation actions. Evidence: Risk response plan, ownership matrix and residual risk review", "Improves decision quality by recognising common judgement biases and using structured analysis to support balanced, evidence-led recommendations. Evidence: Decision-quality reflection, bias identification activity and recommendation rationale", "Links risk governance, assurance and reporting to stakeholder confidence, control discipline and accountable decision-making. Evidence: Risk report, governance review and assurance action log", "Develops facilitation and continuous improvement practice by evaluating risk maturity and identifying improvements to risk management ways of working. Evidence: Risk maturity assessment, facilitated lessons session and improvement plan", "Applies risk identification, qualitative and quantitative assessment, schedule risk and cost risk analysis within an integrated case scenario. Evidence: Case-based risk register, qualitative and quantitative analysis outputs, schedule and cost impact summary", "Consolidates integrated risk reporting, governance, response planning, ownership, residual exposure and continuous improvement through applied case work. Evidence: Integrated risk control pack, governance briefing, response plan and improvement recommendations"]
